voiceover: Can you trust the Bible? This section takes the reliability question apart — here is what you will find. How the text was copied and preserved — from thousands of manuscripts to the Dead Sea Scrolls. Where the Bible meets the real world — archaeology, and the small undesigned coincidences between the accounts. Who wrote the Gospels, how early, and the personal names that fit first-century Palestine. And the hard questions — the alleged contradictions, and how the canon was chosen — raised plainly and answered inside. Every one of these arguments gets a fully-cited deep-dive essay. Each claim is sourced, and the strongest objections are stated fairly, then answered. That is our standard — Checked Before Published. And you will not just read. On every essay an AI tutor answers your questions — ask it anything, or highlight a single sentence and ask about that exact line. Mastery mode lets you explain the argument back in your own words and have it graded. Daily practice brings the key points back just as you are about to forget them. There are pocket cards to share, and a Debate Arena to practise against an AI sceptic before the real conversation. Every essay comes in a plain-English version and a full deep dive, with read-aloud audio. None of this by itself proves the Bible true — that is a further question. What it makes the case for is that the text you hold is essentially what was written: a reliable record to weigh, not a corrupted one. Start anywhere, and follow it where it leads.
